record.original_question: If B={b1,...,br} and B'={b'1,...,b'r} are disjoint bases of a matroid, do there exist permutations of B and B' whose concatenation forms a cyclic ordering in which every r cyclically consecutive elements form a base?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.4. Let B = {b1, . . . , br} and B0 = {b0 1 , . . . , b0 r} be two disjoint bases of a matroid. Then there is a permutation (bπ(1), . . . , bπ(r)) of the elements of B and a permutation (b0 π0(1), . . . , b0 π0(r)) of the elements of B0 such that the combined sequence (bπ(1), . . . , bπ(r), b0 π0(1), . . . , b0 π0(r)) is a cyclic ordering in which every r cyclically consecutive elements form a base.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $r$ on a finite ground set $E$. A cyclic ordering of a finite set $S$ of size $n$ is a bijection from $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ to $S$; a block of $k$ cyclically consecutive elements is the image of any set of $k$ consecutive residues modulo $n$.

Suppose $B = \{b_1, \dots, b_r\}$ and $B' = \{b'_1, \dots, b'_r\}$ are two disjoint bases of $M$ (so $|E| \geq 2r$ and $B \cup B'$ has size $2r$). Restrict $M$ to $B \cup B'$.

Prove or disprove: there exist a permutation $\pi$ of $\{1,\dots,r\}$ and a permutation $\pi'$ of $\{1,\dots,r\}$ such that the sequence
$$(b_{\pi(1)}, b_{\pi(2)}, \dots, b_{\pi(r)}, b'_{\pi'(1)}, b'_{\pi'(2)}, \dots, b'_{\pi'(r)})$$
viewed as a cyclic ordering of $B \cup B'$ has the property that every $r$ cyclically consecutive elements form a basis of $M$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a strengthening of Gabow's conjecture (and related to the Kajitani–Ueno–Miyano conjecture) on cyclic orderability of matroids decomposing into disjoint bases. The general conjecture remains open, but it has been verified for several classes of matroids, including split matroids (2024) and sparse paving matroids.

status_evidence.title: Cyclic ordering of split matroids
status_evidence.snippet: For split matroids, if the ground set decomposes into pairwise disjoint bases, then it is cyclically orderable. This answers a conjecture of Kajitani, Ueno, and Miyano in a special case and strengthens Gabow's conjecture for this class.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is established for split matroids, but remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Cyclic Base Orderings of Matroids (Luo)
status_evidence.snippet: Gabow's conjecture stating that every matroid whose ground set decomposes into two disjoint bases is cyclically orderable.
status_evidence.claim: Gabow's conjecture, of which the stated problem is a strengthening, is still an open problem.
